SYN-PUB-05840.title: Anomaly detection in FDM using autoencoder networks trained exclusively on defect-free layer images
SYN-PUB-05840.text:
Anomaly detection in FDM using autoencoder networks trained exclusively on defect-free layer images (2021, journal, Journal of Quality Engineering in Advanced Manufacturing).
Authors: Saša Kosanović (R0496); Dragan Simić (outside co-author); Olivera Bošković (R0531); Lena Brückner (outside co-author).
Keywords: autoencoder; unsupervised anomaly detection; FDM; reconstruction error; cross-printer.
Standard supervised defect classifiers require large labelled datasets of both normal and anomalous samples. In many production settings, defective prints are rare and costly to produce intentionally. This paper proposes an unsupervised approach using a convolutional autoencoder trained exclusively on 9,600 images of defect-free FDM layers from four different printer models. During inference, reconstruction error is computed per image patch; patches exceeding a threshold calibrated on a held-out normal validation set are flagged as anomalous. On an independent test set of 1,200 images containing five defect categories, the method achieved a detection rate of 84.7% at a false positive rate of 6.3%. Performance degraded by less than 2 percentage points when the model trained on one printer was applied to a different printer of the same manufacturer, suggesting acceptable cross-printer generalisation. The approach reduces annotation burden substantially while maintaining practically useful detection performance.

SYN-PUB-05841.title: Closed-loop extrusion-rate correction driven by in-situ CNN defect signals in FDM
SYN-PUB-05841.text:
Closed-loop extrusion-rate correction driven by in-situ CNN defect signals in FDM (2022, journal, Additive Manufacturing Process Engineering).
Authors: Saša Kosanović (R0496); Bojan Marković (outside co-author); Aleksandar Tešić (outside co-author); Matej Oblak (outside co-author).
Keywords: closed-loop control; extrusion rate; FDM; CNN feedback; tensile strength.
This study presents and evaluates a feedback control strategy that adjusts the extrusion multiplier of an FDM printer in response to defect signals generated by a deployed CNN monitor. The controller reduces the extrusion rate by 2% increments when delamination is detected on two or more consecutive layers, and restores the nominal rate when three consecutive clean layers are observed. Experiments were conducted on an open-architecture FDM platform with firmware modified to accept serial commands from the monitoring module. Sixty-four multi-layer prints of standardised tensile-test coupons in PETG were produced under the closed-loop condition and compared with 64 prints at fixed nominal settings. The closed-loop group showed a 31% reduction in measured delamination area assessed by post-print cross-section imaging and a 9% improvement in mean tensile strength at break. No statistically significant difference in total print time was observed. The work demonstrates the viability of CNN-driven closed-loop process control without requiring a detailed process model.

SYN-PUB-05842.title: Višemodalni pristup praćenju kvaliteta FDM štampe: kombinovanje vizuelnih i akustičnih signala
SYN-PUB-05842.text:
Višemodalni pristup praćenju kvaliteta FDM štampe: kombinovanje vizuelnih i akustičnih signala (2023, conference, Zbornik radova 15. konferencije o inteligentnim sistemima i računarskoj inteligenciji, Subotica).
Authors: Jovana Filipović (outside co-author); Saša Kosanović (R0496); Radomír Šimánek (outside co-author).
Keywords: višemodalno praćenje; akustična emisija; MFCC; FDM; spajanje modaliteta.
Ovaj rad istražuje da li se akustična emisija, snimana mikrofonom postavljenim na okvir štampača, može kombinovati s vizuelnim signalima kamere kako bi se povećala tačnost detekcije grešaka u odnosu na pristup koji se oslanja samo na jedan modalitet. Prikupljeni su simultani audio i video podaci tokom 120 višeslojnih štampi uz namerno unošenje četiri vrste grešaka. Akustični signal je segmentiran na prozore od 0,5 s i opisan melodičnim koeficijentima kepstra (MFCC). Vizuelne karakteristike su dobijene iz prethodno opisane CNN arhitekture. Srednje i kasno spajanje oba modaliteta ispitano je u poređenju s jednomodalnim baznim linijama. Kasno spajanje s naučenim vektorom težina postiglo je makro F1 od 0,89 u poređenju s 0,82 (samo vizuelno) i 0,71 (samo akustično). Rezultati sugerišu da akustični modalitet doprinosi naročito pri detekciji klizanja filamenata, koje je teško vizuelno razlikovati od normalnog površinskog sjaja.

SYN-PUB-05843.title: Benchmark dataset for in-situ FDM layer defect detection: acquisition protocol, annotation guidelines, and baseline results
SYN-PUB-05843.text:
Benchmark dataset for in-situ FDM layer defect detection: acquisition protocol, annotation guidelines, and baseline results (2024, journal, Data in Manufacturing and Process Engineering).
Authors: Saša Kosanović (R0496); Dragan Simić (outside co-author); Lena Brückner (outside co-author); Cristian Moldovan (outside co-author); Radomír Šimánek (outside co-author).
Keywords: benchmark dataset; FDM; layer defects; annotation; mean average precision.
The absence of a standardised, publicly available image dataset has hampered reproducible comparison of in-situ monitoring methods for fused deposition modelling. This paper describes FDMLayerBench, a dataset of 18,400 annotated layer images collected across six printer models, four thermoplastic materials, and twelve print geometries, under three controlled illumination conditions. Defect categories follow a taxonomy of seven types defined in consultation with manufacturing quality engineers. Inter-annotator agreement, measured by Fleiss' kappa, reached 0.81 for major categories and 0.63 for subcategories. Baseline results are reported for five published CNN architectures evaluated under a standardised five-fold cross-validation protocol. The best-performing baseline (a lightweight ResNet variant) achieved a mean average precision of 0.79 across all defect categories. The dataset, annotation tool, and evaluation scripts are released under an open licence to support community benchmarking. Known limitations include an over-representation of PLA material and limited variation in printer manufacturers.

SYN-PUB-05844.title: Lightweight attention-augmented CNN for on-device FDM defect localisation with limited labelled data
SYN-PUB-05844.text:
Lightweight attention-augmented CNN for on-device FDM defect localisation with limited labelled data (2026, journal, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Machine Vision).
Authors: Saša Kosanović (R0496); Aleksandra Nešić (outside co-author); Filip Đorđević (R1034); Miloš Jokić (R0731); Matej Oblak (outside co-author).
Keywords: attention mechanism; semi-supervised learning; embedded CNN; defect localisation; FDM.
Industrial FDM monitoring deployments often face constraints in labelled data volume and computational resources simultaneously. This paper proposes a CNN architecture with a lightweight channel-and-spatial attention module inserted after the third convolutional block, designed to run on embedded hardware while matching the localisation accuracy of heavier models. The architecture has 1.4 million parameters, compared to 11.2 million for the ResNet-18 baseline. Training used a semi-supervised strategy combining 600 labelled and 4,800 unlabelled images via consistency regularisation. On the FDMLayerBench test partition, the proposed model achieved a mean intersection over union of 0.73 for defect region localisation, one point below ResNet-18 (0.74), while reducing inference time from 14 ms to 6 ms on the same embedded hardware. Ablation experiments confirm that the attention module contributes 3.1 points of mean IoU over an equivalent model without attention. Failure cases are concentrated in defect boundaries and thin delamination lines narrower than four pixels.

SYN-PUB-05962.title: Benchmarking Seven Spectral Classifiers for Six-Class Polymer Sorting Under Industrial Noise Conditions
SYN-PUB-05962.text:
Benchmarking Seven Spectral Classifiers for Six-Class Polymer Sorting Under Industrial Noise Conditions (2024, journal, Journal of Analytical and Applied Spectroscopy).
Authors: Aleksandra Đorđević (outside co-author); Nikola Jeremić (outside co-author); Corinna Wehner (outside co-author); Andrea Krstić (R0521); Andrea Kuzmanović (R0506).
Keywords: benchmarking; 1-D CNN; transformer; industrial noise; label noise; open dataset.
Published accuracy figures for NIR polymer classifiers are often obtained under controlled laboratory conditions that do not reflect industrial environments. This paper presents a systematic benchmark of seven classifiers — LDA, k-NN, SVM with RBF kernel, random forest, gradient boosting, a 1-D CNN, and a transformer with 4 attention heads — evaluated on a dataset of 72 000 spectra collected on an operational pilot line with realistic noise sources: vibration, conveyor belt reflectance variation, ambient temperature cycling (18–34 °C), and 6% label noise. Data were split by acquisition day to prevent information leakage. Under these conditions, the 1-D CNN achieved the highest macro F1 of 0.944, followed by the transformer at 0.938 and SVM at 0.931. LDA dropped to 0.871. Training time, inference latency, and memory footprint are reported alongside accuracy. The dataset and evaluation scripts are released under an open licence.

SYN-PUB-06116.title: Reflectance Characteristics of Common Thermoplastics in the 1000–2200 nm Range Under Conveyor Illumination Conditions
SYN-PUB-06116.text:
Reflectance Characteristics of Common Thermoplastics in the 1000–2200 nm Range Under Conveyor Illumination Conditions (2010, journal, Journal of Spectroscopy and Sensor Systems).
Authors: Miroslav Tešić (outside co-author); Helmut Brandauer (outside co-author); Andrea Krstić (R0521).
Keywords: thermoplastics; NIR reflectance; conveyor imaging; linear discriminant analysis; contamination.
This study characterises the diffuse reflectance spectra of six common thermoplastics — HDPE, LDPE, PP, PET, PVC, and PS — measured on a laboratory conveyor rig under halogen line illumination at belt speeds of 0.5–2.0 m/s. A line-scan InGaAs camera with a spectral resolution of 10 nm was used to acquire 1200 spectra per material class under controlled and variable soiling conditions. Spectral preprocessing included standard normal variate correction and Savitzky–Golay smoothing. Principal component analysis showed that the first three components captured 94.7% of interclass variance for clean samples, dropping to 81.3% for samples with 3% surface contamination by mass. A linear discriminant classifier trained on clean data achieved 97.1% accuracy on clean test samples and 88.4% on contaminated ones. The results establish baseline spectral signatures and identify the 1650–1750 nm window as most discriminating for polyolefin separation, providing a practical reference dataset for subsequent classifier development.

SYN-PUB-06117.title: Effect of Belt Speed on Spectral Data Quality in Line-Scan NIR Imaging of Mixed Plastic Flakes
SYN-PUB-06117.text:
Effect of Belt Speed on Spectral Data Quality in Line-Scan NIR Imaging of Mixed Plastic Flakes (2012, conference, Proceedings of the 9th International Conference on Automated Optical Inspection, Zagreb).
Authors: Dragana Vuković (outside co-author); Andrea Krstić (R0521).
Keywords: belt speed; integration time; SNR; line-scan; PET; PP.
Increasing throughput on automated sorting lines requires higher belt speeds, which reduce per-pixel integration time and degrade signal-to-noise ratio in line-scan NIR systems. This work quantifies the relationship between belt speed (0.3–3.5 m/s), integration time (0.1–2.0 ms), and classification accuracy for a binary PET/PP discrimination task using a 256-element InGaAs array. At 2.5 m/s with 0.4 ms integration, SNR fell by 38% relative to the 0.5 m/s reference, and classification accuracy dropped from 96.8% to 89.1% using a fixed LDA model. Adaptive gain scheduling and dark-current correction recovered accuracy to 94.3%. Experiments were conducted with 2 400 flake samples across three size classes (20–50 mm, 50–80 mm, 80–120 mm). The paper provides empirical guidelines for integration-time selection as a function of belt velocity and flake geometry, directly applicable to industrial line design.

SYN-PUB-06118.title: Partial Least Squares Regression for Additive Content Estimation in Recycled Polyolefin Streams
SYN-PUB-06118.text:
Partial Least Squares Regression for Additive Content Estimation in Recycled Polyolefin Streams (2013, journal, Polymer Testing and Analysis).
Authors: Sanja Popović (outside co-author); Lukas Mayer (outside co-author); Andrea Krstić (R0521).
Keywords: PLSR; additive quantification; polyolefin; flame retardants; recycling quality.
Recycled polyolefin batches often contain unknown quantities of flame retardants, plasticisers, and colorants that alter NIR absorption profiles and reduce sorting purity. This study applies partial least squares regression (PLSR) to estimate the concentration of two common additives — decabromodiphenyl ether (0–3% w/w) and dioctyl phthalate (0–5% w/w) — from NIR spectra of HDPE pellet samples. A calibration set of 320 samples with laboratory-verified additive concentrations was used to build PLSR models with 8 and 6 latent variables, respectively. Cross-validated RMSECV values were 0.18% for the brominated additive and 0.31% for the plasticiser. Prediction on an independent set of 80 samples gave RMSEP of 0.22% and 0.38%. The models were robust to pellet colour variation after scatter correction but degraded when carbon-black-pigmented samples exceeded 5% of the batch. Practical implications for quality-control integration in recycling facilities are discussed.

SYN-PUB-06119.title: GPU-Accelerated Spectral Angle Mapping for Real-Time Polymer Classification at 2 m/s Belt Speed
SYN-PUB-06119.text:
GPU-Accelerated Spectral Angle Mapping for Real-Time Polymer Classification at 2 m/s Belt Speed (2016, journal, Mechatronics and Real-Time Systems).
Authors: Nikola Jeremić (outside co-author); Ivan Horvat (outside co-author); Andrea Krstić (R0521).
Keywords: spectral angle mapping; GPU; Jetson; real-time; latency; ejector trigger.
Spectral angle mapping (SAM) is computationally straightforward but rarely benchmarked on embedded GPU hardware for industrial conveyor timing constraints. This paper implements SAM on an NVIDIA Jetson TX1 platform connected to a 320-pixel line-scan NIR camera operating at 1 000 lines/s. The processing pipeline — dark subtraction, flat-field correction, spectral angle computation against a 9-class reference library, and binary ejector trigger generation — was profiled for latency on batches of 1, 4, and 16 simultaneous spectral lines. End-to-end latency from line capture to trigger output was 1.8 ms for single-line mode and 4.1 ms for 16-line batch mode, both within the 8 ms actuation window at 2 m/s. Classification accuracy on 4 500 test flakes across six polymer types was 93.7%. Power consumption was 9.2 W, compatible with 24 V cabinet installation. The implementation is described with enough detail to enable replication.

SYN-PUB-06120.title: Discriminating Black Plastics by Short-Wave NIR Spectroscopy: Carbon Black Interference and Mitigation Strategies
SYN-PUB-06120.text:
Discriminating Black Plastics by Short-Wave NIR Spectroscopy: Carbon Black Interference and Mitigation Strategies (2017, journal, Sensors and Actuators B: Spectral Applications).
Authors: Petra Holzmann (outside co-author); Dragana Vuković (outside co-author); Bojan Simić (outside co-author); Andrea Krstić (R0521).
Keywords: black plastics; carbon black; photoacoustics; time-resolved reflectance; LWIR extension.
Carbon-black-pigmented plastics present a persistent challenge in NIR-based sorting because carbon black strongly absorbs across the entire NIR range, masking polymer-specific overtone bands. This study evaluates three mitigation strategies: (1) extension of the measurement window into the 2200–2500 nm long-wave NIR region where carbon black absorption is relatively lower, (2) photoacoustic excitation at 1064 nm with NIR emission detection, and (3) time-resolved reflectance using a pulsed laser to isolate subsurface signal. Experiments used 180 black-pigmented samples spanning PP, ABS, PA6, and PC with carbon black concentrations of 0.5–4.0% w/w. Long-wave NIR extension improved classification accuracy from 61.3% to 79.4% for the four-class task; photoacoustic detection reached 86.1% but required a 120 ms dwell time, incompatible with high-speed lines. Time-resolved reflectance achieved 82.7% at 12 ms dwell. Practical trade-offs between accuracy and throughput are quantified, and a hybrid sensor layout is proposed.

SYN-PUB-06121.title: Spatial Calibration of Line-Scan NIR Systems for Variable-Thickness Polymer Flakes on Moving Belts
SYN-PUB-06121.text:
Spatial Calibration of Line-Scan NIR Systems for Variable-Thickness Polymer Flakes on Moving Belts (2020, conference, Proceedings of the 14th IFAC Symposium on Robot Control, Novi Sad).
Authors: Nikola Jeremić (outside co-author); Andrea Krstić (R0521).
Keywords: spatial calibration; structured light; thickness correction; segmentation; geometric distortion.
Line-scan NIR cameras acquire spectra along a single spatial axis perpendicular to belt motion. When flakes vary in thickness (1–12 mm), the focal plane offset shifts the effective pixel pitch and introduces geometric distortion in reconstructed hyperspectral images, degrading spatial segmentation prior to per-pixel classification. This paper proposes a structured-light height measurement module mounted upstream of the NIR camera to estimate per-flake thickness and apply a perspective correction to the spectral image in real time. A dataset of 600 flakes with ground-truth thickness measured by contact gauge was used to evaluate calibration accuracy; mean thickness error after correction was 0.4 mm. Integration with a SAM classifier improved segmentation IoU from 0.74 to 0.89 for flakes thicker than 6 mm. The additional processing latency introduced by the correction step was 0.9 ms on the Jetson Xavier platform.

SYN-PUB-06122.title: Online Drift Compensation in NIR Polymer Classifiers Using Unlabelled Production Data
SYN-PUB-06122.text:
Online Drift Compensation in NIR Polymer Classifiers Using Unlabelled Production Data (2021, journal, Computers and Electronics in Industry).
Authors: Marija Lukić (outside co-author); Corinna Wehner (outside co-author); Aleksandra Đorđević (outside co-author); Andrea Krstić (R0521).
Keywords: concept drift; kernel mean matching; unsupervised adaptation; production data; F1 maintenance.
Spectral classifiers deployed on industrial sorting lines experience performance drift over weeks to months due to lamp ageing, lens fouling, and seasonal temperature variation. Periodic manual recalibration is costly and requires line downtime. This paper proposes an unsupervised drift compensation procedure based on kernel mean matching between batches of unlabelled in-production spectra and the original training distribution, updating the classifier's normalisation parameters without requiring new labelled samples. Experiments were conducted on a six-month operational log from a pilot sorting line processing post-consumer packaging, comprising 1.4 million spectra. Without compensation, macro-averaged F1 declined from 0.953 to 0.891 over 24 weeks. With monthly drift compensation triggered automatically when a distribution shift detector exceeded a threshold, F1 was maintained above 0.941 throughout. Computational overhead of the compensation step was less than 2 minutes on a standard industrial PC.

SYN-PUB-06123.title: Identification of PVC in Mixed Post-Consumer Rigids Using a Two-Stage NIR-Raman Decision Fusion Approach
SYN-PUB-06123.text:
Identification of PVC in Mixed Post-Consumer Rigids Using a Two-Stage NIR-Raman Decision Fusion Approach (2022, journal, Resources, Conservation and Recycling).
Authors: Bojan Simić (outside co-author); Lukas Mayer (outside co-author); Tatjana Milošević (outside co-author); Andrea Krstić (R0521).
Keywords: PVC detection; Raman spectroscopy; sensor fusion; decision fusion; contamination control.
PVC contamination in polyolefin recycling streams causes hydrogen chloride emissions during reprocessing and must be removed to below 50 ppm. NIR sorting alone misclassifies PVC as PE at rates up to 4.2% due to spectral overlap near 1730 nm. This paper evaluates a two-stage approach in which a fast NIR pre-screen flags suspect objects for secondary laser Raman interrogation at 785 nm. The NIR stage operated at 2 m/s on a full-width belt; Raman interrogation was triggered only for the 8–12% of items flagged as ambiguous, with a 40 ms dwell. On a test set of 3 200 PVC and 4 800 polyolefin items, the two-stage system achieved PVC recall of 99.2% and precision of 97.8%, compared to 94.3% recall and 96.1% precision for NIR alone. Throughput reduction from Raman dwell was 6.3% at the tested PVC concentration. Cost implications of the additional sensor are discussed.

SYN-PUB-06124.title: Estimating Recycled Content Fraction in Polymer Blends from NIR Spectra Using Conformal Prediction Intervals
SYN-PUB-06124.text:
Estimating Recycled Content Fraction in Polymer Blends from NIR Spectra Using Conformal Prediction Intervals (2025, preprint, arXiv / TechRxiv preprint).
Authors: Andrea Krstić (R0521); Marija Lukić (outside co-author); Dragana Vuković (outside co-author).
Keywords: recycled content; conformal prediction; PLSR; HDPE blend; prediction intervals.
Quantifying the recycled content fraction in a polymer blend is commercially relevant for compliance with EU recycled content targets. This preprint presents a regression approach combining PLSR baseline estimates with conformal prediction to produce statistically valid prediction intervals rather than point estimates. A dataset of 480 HDPE/rHDPE blend samples with recycled content varying from 0 to 100% in 5% increments was prepared gravimetrically. The conformal prediction wrapper, calibrated on 96 samples, produced 90% prediction intervals with empirical coverage of 91.2% on the 120-sample test set. Interval width averaged 8.4 percentage points at 90% confidence. The method is model-agnostic and adds negligible computational cost. Preliminary results suggest that NIR alone can certify recycled content to ±5% only for blends below 30% or above 70% recycled material; intermediate fractions require supplementary measurement. Full data and code are available on the university repository.

SYN-PUB-06125.title: Multi-Line NIR Sensing for Orientation-Independent Classification of Elongated Plastic Profiles on High-Speed Conveyors
SYN-PUB-06125.text:
Multi-Line NIR Sensing for Orientation-Independent Classification of Elongated Plastic Profiles on High-Speed Conveyors (2026, journal, IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement).
Authors: Andrea Krstić (R0521); Bojan Simić (outside co-author); Péter Vásárhelyi (outside co-author); Aleksandra Đorđević (outside co-author).
Keywords: multi-line sensing; elongated profiles; orientation independence; majority vote; PVC; sensor array.
Elongated polymer profiles such as window frame sections and pipe offcuts arrive on sorting conveyors at arbitrary orientations, causing single-line NIR measurements to sample only a narrow cross-section of the object and increasing misclassification for materials with spatially heterogeneous surface coatings. This study evaluates a sensor array of five parallel line-scan NIR cameras spaced 40 mm apart, with their outputs fused by a majority-vote scheme operating on per-object spectra aggregated across all five lines. Experiments used 1 100 elongated profiles across PVC, PP, and fibre-reinforced PA6, arriving at 1.8 m/s with randomised in-plane orientations. The five-line fusion system achieved 96.3% three-class accuracy, compared to 87.1% for the best single-line configuration. False-positive PVC detection rate fell from 3.8% to 0.7%, which is relevant given PVC removal targets. Hardware synchronisation, spatial co-registration of the five cameras, and the added cost relative to accuracy gain are analysed.

SYN-PUB-06127.title: Interpretable Health State Classification for Induction Motor Bearings Using Shapelet-Based Time-Series Features
SYN-PUB-06127.text:
Interpretable Health State Classification for Induction Motor Bearings Using Shapelet-Based Time-Series Features (2025, journal, Journal of Intelligent Maintenance Systems).
Authors: Nemanja Đorđević (outside co-author); Jelena Matić (outside co-author); Andrea Krstić (R0521); Vladana Radić (R0822).
Keywords: shapelets; interpretability; induction motor; bearing health state; time-series classification.
Black-box classifiers for bearing health state estimation are often difficult to validate for deployment in safety-relevant applications. This paper develops an interpretable classification approach based on time-series shapelets—short subsequences whose presence discriminates between health states—extracted from raw vibration waveforms recorded from induction motor bearings under four health states: healthy, early outer-race damage, advanced outer-race damage, and inner-race damage. Shapelet discovery was performed on a training set of 2,400 labelled 0.5-second waveforms. The five most discriminative shapelets achieved 91.3% five-fold cross-validation accuracy using a nearest-shapelet distance classifier. Each shapelet was linked back to physical signal morphology (impacts, modulation patterns) and confirmed by domain-expert inspection. Comparisons with a support vector machine operating on 24 handcrafted spectral features showed equivalent accuracy (91.8%) but the shapelet approach required no manual feature engineering. Shapelet visualisation is shown to facilitate explanation of individual classifications to maintenance technicians.

SYN-PUB-06388.title: Few-shot surface defect detection on reflective metal parts
SYN-PUB-06388.text:
Few-shot surface defect detection on reflective metal parts (2024, journal, Journal of Industrial Vision).
Authors: Jovana Milovanović (outside co-author); Gregor Vesel (outside co-author); Nikola Stojanović (R0548); Tamara Đurić (outside co-author).
Detecting surface defects on highly reflective metal components remains a significant challenge for automated visual inspection systems, primarily because specular reflections obscure subtle anomalies and corrupt standard feature representations. This paper presents a few-shot learning framework tailored specifically to reflective surfaces, combining a reflection-aware preprocessing pipeline with a prototypical network backbone trained on a curated set of metallic defect categories. A novel data augmentation strategy simulates varying illumination angles and reflection intensities, substantially increasing intra-class diversity without requiring large annotated datasets. The proposed method is evaluated on a newly introduced benchmark—ReflectDefect-M—comprising five metallic material types and twelve defect classes, collected in cooperation with regional SME manufacturing partners. Experimental results demonstrate that the framework achieves a mean average precision of 87.3% using only five support examples per defect class, outperforming seven competitive baselines by margins ranging from 4.1 to 11.6 percentage points. Ablation studies confirm the contribution of each pipeline stage. The work establishes a practical pathway for deploying few-shot defect detectors in small-batch production settings where collecting large labeled datasets is economically infeasible.

SYN-PUB-06389.title: Quantized detectors for real-time inspection on edge devices
SYN-PUB-06389.text:
Quantized detectors for real-time inspection on edge devices (2023, conference, Embedded AI Conference).
Authors: Nikola Stojanović (R0548); Rastko Petrović (outside co-author); Lena Hofmann (outside co-author); Miloš Cvejić (outside co-author).
Real-time visual inspection on embedded and edge hardware demands detectors that are simultaneously accurate and computationally lean. This paper investigates the application of post-training and quantization-aware training techniques to a family of convolutional defect detectors intended for deployment on low-power edge devices used in industrial conveyor-line inspection. We evaluate INT8 and mixed-precision INT4/INT8 quantization strategies across four detector architectures, measuring the trade-off between inference latency, memory footprint, and detection accuracy on three public industrial defect benchmarks. A structured pruning step preceding quantization is shown to recover accuracy losses for the most aggressive quantization settings. On a representative ARM Cortex-M55 target platform, the best-performing quantized detector achieves 34 frames per second with less than 2% mAP degradation relative to the full-precision baseline, satisfying the real-time constraint of most conveyor inspection scenarios. We further provide deployment guidelines and an open-source model-conversion toolkit compatible with common edge inference runtimes, lowering the barrier for practitioners in small and medium manufacturing enterprises to adopt AI-based inspection.

SYN-PUB-06390.title: Synthetic defect generation for visual quality control
SYN-PUB-06390.text:
Synthetic defect generation for visual quality control (2022, journal, Machine Vision Applications Review).
Authors: Nikola Stojanović (R0548); Jovana Milovanović (outside co-author); Aleksandar Vuković (outside co-author); Petra Kovačević (outside co-author).
The scarcity of labeled defect images is a persistent bottleneck in training robust visual quality control models, particularly for rare or newly introduced defect types. This paper explores procedural and generative approaches to synthetic defect generation, proposing a unified pipeline that combines physically based rendering (PBR) with a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) fine-tuned on a small set of real defect exemplars. The pipeline produces photorealistic defect images across six categories—scratches, pits, cracks, stains, delamination, and inclusion—on both metallic and polymer substrates. A systematic evaluation protocol measures the downstream impact of synthetic augmentation on detection model performance using three standard industrial datasets. Models trained with a 70% synthetic / 30% real mixture achieve accuracy within 3.2% of fully supervised baselines trained on complete real datasets, while reducing annotation effort by approximately 80%. The study also benchmarks the realism of generated images using FID and a domain-expert perceptual rating study. The findings support synthetic data generation as a cost-effective strategy for bootstrapping quality control systems in low-data manufacturing environments.

SYN-PUB-06391.title: Adaptive anomaly detection for multi-product assembly lines using one-class contrastive learning
SYN-PUB-06391.text:
Adaptive anomaly detection for multi-product assembly lines using one-class contrastive learning (2024, journal, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics).
Authors: Jovana Milovanović (outside co-author); Dragana Ilić (outside co-author); Nikola Stojanović (R0548); Stefan Brandt (outside co-author).
Keywords: anomaly detection; one-class learning; contrastive learning; multi-product inspection; edge inference.
Modern assembly lines frequently switch between product variants, requiring inspection systems that adapt rapidly to new normal-appearance distributions without collecting defect examples in advance. This paper presents an adaptive one-class contrastive learning framework for unsupervised anomaly detection in multi-product settings. The approach uses a momentum-updated reference encoder and an online memory bank of normal embeddings that is refreshed at product changeover events, enabling the model to track appearance shifts without full retraining. A self-supervised pretext task based on synthetic local masking strengthens the encoder's sensitivity to subtle textural and structural anomalies. The framework is evaluated on a novel multi-variant industrial benchmark—PolyAssembly-7—covering seven polymer component types across four product families. It achieves an average AUROC of 93.1% across all variants and demonstrates adaptation in fewer than 50 unlabeled normal samples per changeover, outperforming five established one-class detection baselines. Inference runs at 28 fps on an NVIDIA Jetson edge module. The results highlight the viability of continual anomaly detection for flexible manufacturing without persistent human annotation effort.

SYN-PUB-06392.title: Knowledge distillation for lightweight surface inspection models on heterogeneous edge hardware
SYN-PUB-06392.text:
Knowledge distillation for lightweight surface inspection models on heterogeneous edge hardware (2023, journal, Journal of Real-Time Image Processing).
Authors: Nikola Stojanović (R0548); Rastko Petrović (outside co-author); Lena Hofmann (outside co-author).
Keywords: knowledge distillation; edge computing; model compression; surface inspection; heterogeneous hardware.
Deploying high-accuracy surface inspection models on heterogeneous edge hardware—spanning microcontrollers, FPGAs, and GPU-equipped single-board computers—requires models that balance computational cost with detection performance across very different hardware profiles. This paper proposes a hardware-aware knowledge distillation pipeline in which a large teacher network transfers representational knowledge to a suite of student architectures of varying capacities, each targeting a specific hardware tier. A novel attention-alignment distillation loss aligns intermediate feature maps at multiple scales, preserving fine-grained defect discriminability in the student networks. Experiments on three industrial surface inspection datasets show that the distilled lightweight students retain 95–98% of teacher mAP while reducing multiply-accumulate operations by 4× to 11× depending on the target hardware. We further present a hardware profiling methodology that automates student architecture selection given user-defined latency and accuracy constraints. The complete pipeline is released as an open-source toolkit, enabling non-expert practitioners to generate inspection-ready models for their specific edge deployment targets.

SYN-PUB-06393.title: Domain randomization strategies for cross-industry transfer in visual defect detection
SYN-PUB-06393.text:
Domain randomization strategies for cross-industry transfer in visual defect detection (2022, journal, Computer Vision and Image Understanding).
Authors: Nikola Stojanović (R0548); Petra Kovačević (outside co-author); Aleksandar Vuković (outside co-author); Marc Delacroix (outside co-author).
Keywords: domain randomization; transfer learning; defect detection; synthetic data; industrial inspection.
Visual defect detection models trained on one industrial domain often fail to generalize when transferred to a different material type, surface finish, or manufacturing process. This paper systematically investigates domain randomization as a transfer-enabling strategy, examining how randomization of texture, illumination, background clutter, and camera parameters during synthetic training data generation affects cross-domain transferability. A large-scale factorial experiment is conducted across six source-target domain pairs spanning metallic, ceramic, and textile substrates. Results show that targeted randomization of illumination direction and surface reflectance parameters yields the largest gains in target-domain detection accuracy, while excessive geometric randomization can degrade performance. Building on these findings, we propose an adaptive randomization curriculum that progressively increases domain diversity during training, guided by a domain-gap estimator computed from unlabeled target samples. The curriculum approach achieves a 6.8% average mAP improvement over static randomization across all transfer pairs, demonstrating a principled path toward generalizable industrial vision systems that require minimal target-domain labeling.

SYN-PUB-06394.title: Temporal consistency regularization for video-based industrial anomaly detection
SYN-PUB-06394.text:
Temporal consistency regularization for video-based industrial anomaly detection (2021, conference, International Conference on Machine Vision and Applications (ICMVA)).
Authors: Nikola Stojanović (R0548); Tamara Đurić (outside co-author); Ivana Radovanović (outside co-author).
Keywords: anomaly detection; video inspection; temporal consistency; industrial vision; recurrent networks.
Frame-level anomaly detectors applied to industrial video streams often produce temporally inconsistent predictions, flagging and clearing the same defect region across successive frames due to minor illumination or motion changes. This paper introduces a temporal consistency regularization scheme that enforces smooth anomaly score trajectories across video frames without requiring ground-truth temporal annotations. A recurrent scoring head aggregates frame-level embeddings over a short sliding window, and a consistency loss penalizes abrupt score oscillations that are inconsistent with the physical persistence of genuine defects. The approach is evaluated on a new video inspection dataset—ConveyorVID—capturing three product types under realistic factory floor conditions including vibration, partial occlusion, and varying conveyor speed. The regularized model reduces the false-positive rate by 31% and improves temporal F1 score by 8.4 points compared to a strong frame-level baseline, with a negligible increase in computational overhead. Qualitative results confirm that the detector maintains stable anomaly localization across frames, a property that is critical for downstream alarm-triggering logic in automated quality control systems.

SYN-PUB-06396.title: Active learning with model uncertainty sampling for efficient annotation in industrial inspection pipelines
SYN-PUB-06396.text:
Active learning with model uncertainty sampling for efficient annotation in industrial inspection pipelines (2021, journal, International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology).
Authors: Nikola Stojanović (R0548); Dragana Ilić (outside co-author); Gregor Vesel (outside co-author).
Keywords: active learning; annotation efficiency; defect detection; model uncertainty; industrial inspection.
Labeling defect images in industrial settings is expensive and requires domain expertise, making the efficient allocation of annotation effort a critical practical concern. This paper proposes an active learning framework for industrial defect detection that uses ensemble-based model uncertainty to prioritize the most informative unlabeled samples for expert annotation. A Monte Carlo dropout ensemble estimates epistemic uncertainty at the instance and region levels, and a diversity-aware sampling strategy prevents the selection of redundant near-duplicate crops from the same production batch. The framework is integrated into a realistic annotation pipeline validated with two industrial partners producing metal stampings and injection-molded plastic components. Across both domains, the active learning approach achieves 90% of fully supervised baseline performance using only 35% of the total available labeled data, reducing annotation cost by an estimated 58% in practitioner time. A user study with three quality control engineers confirms that the uncertainty-guided sample ordering significantly reduces the cognitive load of the labeling process compared to random sample presentation.

SYN-PUB-06937.title: Gradient-based edge detection performance on low-contrast food packaging under variable conveyor illumination
SYN-PUB-06937.text:
Gradient-based edge detection performance on low-contrast food packaging under variable conveyor illumination (2015, journal, Journal of Manufacturing and Automation Research).
Authors: Ksenija Ranković (R0602); Miroslav Tešić (outside co-author); Ivan Marković (R0840); Dragana Vuković (outside co-author).
Keywords: edge detection; conveyor vision; illumination; embedded ARM; food packaging inspection.
This paper evaluates four gradient-based edge detectors—Sobel, Prewitt, Scharr and a tuned Canny implementation—applied to grey-scale images of plastic food containers acquired on a laboratory conveyor belt running at speeds between 0.3 and 1.2 m/s. Illumination was varied systematically using diffuse dome lighting, coaxial lighting and combined side-plus-coaxial setups. A dataset of 4 200 images was collected across six packaging types. Edge continuity, F1 score against manually annotated ground truth, and processing latency on an ARM Cortex-A9 processor were measured. The Scharr operator combined with adaptive histogram equalisation achieved the highest mean F1 of 0.83 at 1.0 m/s under coaxial illumination, at a frame throughput of 47 fps. Diffuse dome lighting reduced F1 variance across packaging colours by 18% compared with single-source setups. The results provide practical guidance for lighting selection in low-budget inline inspection cells without dedicated machine-vision controllers.

SYN-PUB-06939.title: Pose estimation accuracy for randomly oriented small metallic parts on a moving belt using structured-light depth sensing
SYN-PUB-06939.text:
Pose estimation accuracy for randomly oriented small metallic parts on a moving belt using structured-light depth sensing (2020, journal, Robotics and Flexible Manufacturing Systems).
Authors: Ksenija Ranković (R0602); Dragana Vuković (outside co-author); Sándor Fekete (outside co-author).
Keywords: pose estimation; structured light; metallic parts; point-pair features; robotic grasping.
This study assesses the suitability of a low-cost structured-light depth sensor for estimating the 6-DOF pose of small metallic workpieces on a conveyor belt moving at 0.4 m/s. Eighty part instances across four geometry classes were tested; each class included reflective surfaces that are known to produce depth artefacts in time-of-flight and structured-light sensors. A preprocessing step using infrared-band filtering and surface normal smoothing reduced invalid pixel ratios from 31% to 9%. Pose estimation used a point-pair feature algorithm with a RANSAC verification stage. Mean position error was 1.8 mm and mean orientation error was 2.3° over 2 400 trials. A downstream six-axis collaborative arm successfully grasped parts in 91.4% of trials at the given belt speed. The paper quantifies the dependence of pose error on part shininess measured by a calibrated reflectance standard and discusses the minimum acceptable surface roughness for reliable sensing.

SYN-PUB-06940.title: Synchronisation of image acquisition and robot trajectory planning in a dual-arm pick-and-place cell
SYN-PUB-06940.text:
Synchronisation of image acquisition and robot trajectory planning in a dual-arm pick-and-place cell (2021, conference, European Conference on Robotics and Mechatronics (ECRM)).
Authors: Ksenija Ranković (R0602); Nemanja Ćirić (outside co-author); Ivan Polić (outside co-author).
Keywords: dual-arm robotics; EtherCAT; trajectory synchronisation; pick-and-place; ROS 2.
Coordinating two six-axis arms sharing a single conveyor pick zone requires tight synchronisation between the vision system's object-position updates and each arm's trajectory planner. This paper presents a time-stamped message-passing architecture implemented over EtherCAT that allows position corrections to be injected into a running trajectory up to 35 ms before the arm reaches the pick point. Experiments were conducted with 12 object types of varying size and aspect ratio at conveyor speeds of 0.5 and 0.9 m/s. The dual-arm cell achieved a combined throughput of 58 picks per minute with a collision-free rate of 99.7% over 10 000 continuous operating cycles. Cycle time improved by 22% compared with a token-passing arbitration baseline. Latency budgets for each pipeline stage—capture, classification, coordinate transform, trajectory update—are reported individually. The architecture was implemented on a ROS 2-based controller running on a real-time Linux kernel.

SYN-PUB-06941.title: Comparison of lightweight CNN architectures for real-time object sorting on an NVIDIA Jetson platform
SYN-PUB-06941.text:
Comparison of lightweight CNN architectures for real-time object sorting on an NVIDIA Jetson platform (2022, journal, Journal of Real-Time Image Processing and Embedded Systems).
Authors: Ksenija Ranković (R0602); Milena Stojanović (outside co-author); Andrej Kovačević (outside co-author); Tomáš Novotný (outside co-author).
Keywords: lightweight CNN; Jetson Xavier; TensorRT; recycling sorter; embedded inference; INT8 quantisation.
This paper benchmarks five lightweight convolutional architectures—MobileNetV2, EfficientNet-B0, SqueezeNet 1.1, ShuffleNetV2 and a custom four-block network designed for the task—on an NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX module used as an embedded sorter controller. The test scenario involves classifying thirteen categories of mixed municipal recyclables on a conveyor running at 0.7 m/s, where objects may overlap partially. A dataset of 26 000 labelled single-object images and 8 400 partially occluded multi-object frames was assembled in-house. TensorRT-optimised INT8 models were compared on throughput, top-1 accuracy and power draw. EfficientNet-B0 achieved 88.4% top-1 accuracy at 68 fps and 9.1 W; the custom network reached 85.1% at 94 fps and 7.4 W. Occlusion degraded accuracy by 8–14 percentage points depending on architecture. The paper discusses trade-offs relevant to selecting a model for battery-powered or thermally constrained inspection units.

SYN-PUB-06942.title: Dataset and baseline results for curved-surface 2D code detection under industrial lighting conditions
SYN-PUB-06942.text:
Dataset and baseline results for curved-surface 2D code detection under industrial lighting conditions (2026, preprint, arXiv (cs.CV)).
Authors: Milena Stojanović (outside co-author); Tomáš Novotný (outside co-author); Ksenija Ranković (R0602); Darija Pejić (outside co-author).
Keywords: dataset; 2D code detection; QR code; DataMatrix; curved surface; industrial imaging.
Publicly available datasets for 2D code (QR and DataMatrix) detection on curved surfaces are scarce, and those that exist rarely include the range of industrial lighting conditions encountered in practice. This preprint describes a dataset of 11 400 images collected on cylindrical, conical and saddle-shaped surfaces under eight distinct lighting configurations, including high-pressure sodium emulation, LED ring, telecentric backlight and mixed ambient. Images were captured at three conveyor speeds (0, 0.6 and 1.1 m/s) with two camera models. Each image is annotated with code location polygons, surface curvature class, lighting type and belt speed. Baseline detection results are reported for four open-source pipelines. ZXing-C++ achieved the highest overall decode rate of 81.3%, dropping to 64.7% on saddle surfaces. The dataset is released under a CC BY 4.0 licence and is intended to support reproducible comparison of detection methods in this under-studied setting.

W4206192560.title: Extraction and classification of apple defects under uneven illumination based on machine vision
W4206192560.text: Journal of Food Process Engineering, 2022. Abstract The extraction and classification of different kinds of defects can achieve a more sophisticated classification of apples. In this study, a region of interest (ROI) extraction algorithm based on background separation, brightness correction, and the global threshold was designed for the extraction of apple decay and bruise under uneven light conditions. After brightness correction, we calculate the average gray value of the apple region and multiply the value by 0.8 as the threshold. In this way, the threshold of different apple images can be determined automatically without a manual setting. After extracting ROI, we realized the classification of the two kinds of defects by extracting texture features. Based on the selected texture features, the support vector machine discriminant models were established. The accuracy of the model based on angular second moment was 94.8% and the model based on entropy was 94.7%. The total time from ROI extraction to classification was approximately 1.2 s. The results showed that this extraction and classification process had application prospects in practical detection classification. W4304128474.title: Real-Time Grading of Defect Apples Using Semantic Segmentation Combination with a Pruned YOLO V4 Network
W4304128474.text: Foods, 2022. At present, the apple grading system usually conveys apples by a belt or rollers. This usually leads to low hardness or expensive fruits being bruised, resulting in economic losses. In order to realize real-time detection and classification of high-quality apples, separate fruit trays were designed to convey apples and used to prevent apples from being bruised during image acquisition. A semantic segmentation method based on the BiSeNet V2 deep learning network was proposed to segment the defective parts of defective apples. BiSeNet V2 for apple defect detection obtained a slightly better result in MPA with a value of 99.66%, which was 0.14 and 0.19 percentage points higher than DAnet and Unet, respectively. A model pruning method was used to optimize the structure of the YOLO V4 network. The detection accuracy of defect regions in apple images was further improved by the pruned YOLO V4 network. Then, a surface mapping method between the defect area in apple images and the actual defect area was proposed to accurately calculate the defect area. Finally, apples on separate fruit trays were sorted according to the number and area of defects in the apple images. The experimental results showed that the average accuracy of apple classification was 92.42%, and the F1 score was 94.31. In commercial separate fruit tray grading and sorting machines, it has great application potential.
